schema.note: The eval test set. Axis A measures whether lifecycle prompt injection reaches the artifact; axis B measures what a plugin skill adds over the shipped CLI prompts alone.

case_fields.stage: axis A only: the lifecycle stage the case works
case_fields.skill: axis B only: the skill the case is about; 'cross-axis' where the scenario spans several
case_fields.invokes: the skill directory the case invokes, or a list where the scenario genuinely spans several. This is what evals/coverage.py subtracts from the shipped skill set.
case_fields.item: which seeded fixture item the case acts on: 'backlog', 'active', 'completed', or absent where the case creates its own
case_fields.prompt: what the agent is given. '{item}' is substituted with the minted slug of the item named in 'item', since the CLI mints date-prefixed slugs and they cannot be hardcoded.
case_fields.arms: which arms the case runs. Axis A: 'customized' (the node carrying work.lifecycle.stages and the nonces) and 'control' (the same seeder with that block omitted). Axis B: 'with-skill' and 'no-skill'.
case_fields.runner: present only where the case is runner-specific; absent means the default runner
case_fields.fixture: optional; a named fixture variant ('customized', 'control' or 'bare') used in every arm of the case, overriding the per-axis default. Only 'bare' is used today.
case_fields.assertions: each entry either names a predicate from 'predicates' below, or carries an 'unmechanized' marker

assertion_fields.predicate: a name from the 'predicates' vocabulary below
assertion_fields.arm: optional; the assertion is evaluated only in this arm. Absent means every arm the case runs.
assertion_fields.text: the human-readable claim, copied into grading.json
assertion_fields.unmechanized: present instead of 'predicate' where the spec's assertion cannot be expressed in either grader family. The claim is recorded so it is not silently dropped, and is reported as unmechanized rather than as a pass or a fail.
assertion_fields.why: required alongside 'unmechanized': why neither grader family can express it

transcript_blocks_present.reads: both injected blocks appear in the resolved stage prompt and are non-empty, identified by their headings ('## Lifecycle stage contract', '## Stage instructions') rather than by content, which varies per node. A heading with nothing under it is a fail.

transcript_gate_before_artifact.reads: a `tcw work stage gate` invocation appears in the transcript before the stage artifact is written

transcript_fallback_commands_run.reads: the composing skill's fenced fallback commands were run by hand. Codex only (I7).

transcript_contains.reads: the literal text appears in the transcript
transcript_contains.confirmed: Not among the three transcript reads task 6 enumerates. Confirmed as an expansion rather than inherited silently: it is the same machinery as the listed reads, and A4 cannot be stated without it now that the skill binding carries no nonce. A general ordering read would be the same kind of step and is deliberately still not taken, so B8 stays unmechanized.

transcript_absent.reads: the literal text appears nowhere in the transcript
transcript_absent.confirmed: Not among the three transcript reads task 6 enumerates. Confirmed as an expansion rather than inherited silently: it is the same machinery as the listed reads, and A4 cannot be stated without it now that the skill binding carries no nonce. A general ordering read would be the same kind of step and is deliberately still not taken, so B8 stays unmechanized.

tool_input_contains.reads: the literal text appears in the input of some tool call the agent made (a `Read` file path, a `Bash` command, and so on). Ignores assistant text, user messages and tool results, so a path a loaded skill merely mentions does not count as opened.

tool_input_absent.reads: the literal text appears in the input of no tool call the agent made. Ignores assistant text, user messages and tool results. Fails with 'no tool calls found' when the transcript has no tool calls at all, so an unrecognised transcript shape cannot pass it.

nonce_in_artifact.reads: the nonce recorded in the node root's manifest.json for that binding kind appears in that artifact. Reported with provenance: injected, fallback-sourced, or unknown. A nonce whose provenance cannot be established is never reported as a pass.

nonce_absent_from_artifact.reads: none of the named kinds' nonces appear in that artifact

stage_prompt_empty.reads: `tcw work stage prompt <stage> <item>` resolves to zero bytes on the node

stage_prompt_bookended.reads: `tcw work stage prompt <stage> <item>` resolves to non-empty text carrying the bookend

artifact_exists.reads: the named artifact exists on the item and is non-empty

item_status.reads: the item's status via `tcw work show`

new_item_count.reads: how many work items exist beyond the seeded set, via `tcw work list`

capability_status.reads: the capability's status via `tcw capabilities show`

new_capability_count.reads: how many capabilities exist beyond the seeded set

taxonomy_entry_kind.reads: a taxonomy entry with that id exists and is of that kind ('vocabulary' or 'feature')

taxonomy_feature_links_vocab.reads: the feature declares that vocabulary term in its vocab links

validate_exit_zero.reads: `tcw validate` exits 0 on the node at end state

git_order.reads: in `git log --oneline`, the first commit whose subject matches 'before' precedes the first matching 'after'. Ordering only: identical commits result from compliant and non-compliant histories, so the log cannot establish which tool wrote them.

git_commit_per_artifact.reads: each lifecycle artifact the run produced landed in its own commit

files_changed_exactly.reads: the working tree (committed, uncommitted and untracked non-ignored files) differs from the seeded commit in exactly these paths. The seeded commit is `seeded_head` in timing.json; a run recorded without it fails. Says which files changed, not whether the change was any good.

cases.prompt: Work the spec stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the `file` binding's nonce reaches spec.md (I2, I3, I4)

the control produces a well-formed spec.md. A baseline artifact, not a discriminator: a 16-character random nonce cannot appear in the control, so this arm only tells 'the nonce is absent and the artifact is otherwise fine' apart from 'the run fell over'.
the node still validates

cases.prompt: Work the plan stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the `blob` binding's nonce reaches plan.md (I4)
the control produces a well-formed plan.md. Baseline, not a discriminator.
the node still validates

cases.prompt: Work the implement stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the `generate` binding's computed nonce reaches outcome.md (I4). It is in no committed TCW file, so it cannot come from repository knowledge or from training; the script itself is readable from inside the node, so this is not a claim that an agent could not have produced it another way.
the control produces a well-formed outcome.md. Baseline, not a discriminator.
the node still validates

cases.prompt: Work the verify stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the resolved prompt carries the `skill` binding's pointer line and the transcript shows the agent read it. Not a nonce check: `_resolve_one` resolves a `skill` binding to the literal `Invoke the <name> skill.` and never reads the skill's body, so no nonce can travel this path.
the control carries no such pointer line — this is the one axis A case where the control is the discriminator
the verify stage produced its artifact

assertions.unmechanized: the agent acted on the pointer rather than merely echoing it
assertions.why: a `SKILL.md` inside a throwaway fixture node is not a registered skill under any harness, so there is nothing for the agent to reach. This pass makes no claim beyond whether it tries.

cases.prompt: Work the postmortem stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the silence opt-out resolves to zero bytes
the control resolves to the bookended builtin floor. Assert the shape, not a byte count: the floor moves whenever a builtin prompt is edited.
silence invents nothing: none of the other stages' nonces appear in the post-mortem (I5)

cases.note: Invokes the generic composer, not `post-mortem`. I5 asks what an agent does with a stage that asks nothing: proceed on the router alone, or invent instructions to fill the gap. The router is the composing skill's first block, so the composer is what has to be in play. `post-mortem` stays covered by B9. The two stage-prompt checks look like duplicates of the fixture guard and are not. The guard reads a freshly seeded node; these read the node after the agent has worked it, under acceptEdits, where the agent could have edited tcw-config.yaml. They confirm the stage was still silent for this run, which is the only form of the claim that grading can make. Both predicates therefore keep their only user.

cases.prompt: Work the spec stage for {item}.

assertions.text: both injected blocks are present and non-empty (I1, I2)

cases.note: Single-arm by correction. `bookend` is applied whenever the resolved text is non-empty, so it wraps the builtin floor in the control exactly as it wraps bound text in the treatment: both blocks render in both arms and there is no cross-arm contrast to read. This is an absolute reading, not a delta. The stage is `spec`, not 'any' — under `postmortem` the second block is empty in the treatment by design and would read as failure mode I2 for a reason that is not a defect.

cases.prompt: Work the spec stage for {item}.

assertions.text: `tcw work stage gate` ran before the artifact was written (I6). Observed, not attributed: both arms carry the bookend, so the bookend is not the variable and this may not be reported as the bookend's doing.

cases.note: Single-arm for the same reason as A6: the gate reminder is present in both arms.

cases.prompt: Work the spec stage for {item}.

assertions.text: the manual fallback commands were run by hand (I7)
the `file` nonce reached spec.md. Under Codex this is expected to be fallback-sourced rather than injected, which is exactly what the provenance field exists to say.

cases.prompt: Users keep asking to get their report data out of demo-app as a CSV so they can drop it in a spreadsheet. Can you build that? The report rendering all lives in src/reports.py.

assertions.text: one work item was created for the request
the item was planned, not just filed

`tcw work start` preceded the first code commit The `before` pattern is the transition commit's actual subject shape, `tcw work: <slug> → active`. The literal word `start` never appears in it, so matching on that would fail every run regardless of what the agent did.
each lifecycle artifact landed in its own commit
the node still validates

cases.prompt: there's a thing sitting in docs/work/inbox/slow-login.md, deal with it

assertions.text: the inbox entry was accepted into one tracked item
the accepted item landed in the backlog
the node still validates

assertions.unmechanized: the minted title and tags are sensible for the request
assertions.why: judging a title as sensible is a reading of prose against intent. The mechanical half is that tags come from the registered set, which `tcw validate` already enforces, so a separate predicate would add nothing.

cases.prompt: The invoice download work in {item} is finished and committed. Close it out.

assertions.text: the ledger was flipped Missing → Supported
the item completed
the completion gate was satisfied rather than forced
the node still validates

cases.prompt: Our billing code keeps using words nobody has written down. A statement run is the nightly job in src/billing.py that produces every customer's statement; dunning is the retry sequence we go through after a charge fails. Get both of those on the record properly — the statement run is something the system does, not just a word.

assertions.text: dunning was registered as Vocabulary
the statement run was registered as a Feature, not as Vocabulary
the Feature links the vocabulary it operates on
`tcw validate` is clean
recording new terms in a project that already uses TCW is taxonomy work, so no setup document was opened

cases.prompt: I want users to be able to email a report to themselves from demo-app. Which axis does that belong in, and where do I start?

assertions.text: the answer names the capabilities axis, which is where a new user-facing ability belongs
an orientation question was answered, not acted on

assertions.unmechanized: the orientation is actually good — it routes to the right axis for the right reason and tells the user where to start
assertions.why: quality of an explanation is a judgment about prose. Neither grader family reads meaning; the substring check above says the word appeared, not that the answer was right. This is the clearest case in the set for a human read of the two transcripts side by side.

cases.prompt: `tcw work complete` just threw a traceback at me instead of completing the item. Looks like a bug in tcw itself. What do I do with this?

assertions.text: no local work item was created — logging a TCW bug as local project work is the natural wrong answer this skill exists to prevent
the agent routed the report upstream to the TCW repository

cases.note: The sharpest negative case in the set: passing means the agent did not do the obvious thing.

cases.prompt:
Here are the four open issues on demo-app. Triage them for me.

#11 "CSV export drops the last row" — reproducible, one-line off-by-one in src/reports.py.
#12 "Invoice download 404s for annual plans" — reproducible against billing.
#13 "Can you add dark mode, also please rewrite this in Rust" — no.
#14 "thanks, great tool" — not a bug.

assertions.text: only the two actionable issues became work items
the node still validates

assertions.unmechanized: a reply was offered for every issue, including the two that were not converted
assertions.why: this needs a per-issue reading of the transcript's prose — whether a proposed reply exists, and is addressed to that issue. The transcript family does substring and command-ordering reads, not per-entity prose attribution.

cases.note: The issue set is supplied inline in the prompt rather than seeded, because the fixture node has no GitHub remote and the harness has no network. This measures the triage judgement, not the `gh` plumbing the skill would normally drive — recorded as a narrowing of the spec's scenario. Narrowed deliberately: the fixture node has no GitHub remote and the harness has no network, so the skill's `gh` plumbing is unreachable. The four issues are supplied inline in the prompt, two actionable and two not. This measures triage judgement, not the plumbing.

cases.prompt: We're adding scheduled report delivery to demo-app: a user picks a report and a cadence, and it lands in their inbox on that schedule. Nothing about this exists yet — not the word, not the ability, not the work. Set it up.

assertions.text: a capability was declared for the new ability
a work item was created for the build
the node still validates, which is what catches a capability referencing a Feature that was never registered
"Set it up" here asks for a term, a capability and a work item in a project that already uses TCW, so no setup document was opened

assertions.unmechanized: the three axes were touched in the right order — the term registered before the capability that uses it, the capability declared before the work item that delivers it
assertions.why: the end state shows all three exist, not the sequence in which they were created: within one agent run they can land in a single commit or none. Recovering the sequence needs a general command-ordering read of the transcript, and the grader defines only one specific ordering read (`tcw work stage gate` before the artifact). See the report note — this one is close to expressible and would become so if the transcript family gained a general ordering predicate.

cases.prompt: {item} shipped, and then we found that it never handled the empty-report case at all — src/reports.py blows up on a customer with no invoices. Which stage should have caught that?

assertions.text: a post-mortem was written against the completed item
the post-mortem analysed rather than silently opening follow-up work

assertions.unmechanized: the stage named is the earliest stage that could in fact have caught the defect
assertions.why: this is the finding the skill exists to produce and it is a judgement about the item's own history. A predicate could check that some stage was named; it cannot check that the right one was.

cases.prompt: I fixed the off-by-one in src/reports.py that was dropping the last row of every CSV export. Anything else this needs before I call it done?

assertions.text: the declared documentation entries were touched and nothing else was

assertions.unmechanized: the entries were updated correctly — the changelog line describes this fix, and the README change is warranted
assertions.why: the path list says which files changed, not whether the edit was any good. The 'no others' half of the spec's assertion is mechanical; the 'the right entries' half is only mechanical as far as the filenames.

cases.note: The seeder declares exactly README.md and docs/changelogs/upcoming.md, so the path list reconciles. src/reports.py is deliberately not listed: the fix the prompt describes is not in the seeded fixture, and the check compares against the seeded commit, so src/reports.py would only appear if the agent edited a file the user says is already fixed.

cases.prompt: Set up documentation tracking so README.md is also updated whenever any code in demo-app changes.

assertions.text: the agent opened the configure skill's docs-sync.md, the document for declaring documentation entries
the agent did not open any setup document: "set up" here names a configuration area in a project that already uses TCW
only tcw-config.yaml changed: README.md already exists, so the entry is new and nothing needs creating
`tcw validate` is clean, so the new entry parses

cases.note: The fixture declares README.md only under Public-API (evals/seed_fixture.py, _declare_documentation). The request adds a second (path, trigger) pair for the same file, under Any-Code-Change or a project-defined trigger, so the agent has no reason to create a file. In the no-skill arm no plugin is loaded, so no skill document can be opened: the contains check is expected to fail there and the absent check passes trivially. That difference is what the case measures. docs-sync.md tells the agent to ask which form, files, trigger and description to use; the prompt already names the file and when it must change, so an agent that still stops to ask has routed correctly but fails files_changed_exactly. Read those two checks separately when grading. A second way a correct route fails files_changed_exactly: docs-sync.md's "Create Tracked Files" step can lead the agent to create docs/release-notes/upcoming.md, which the fixture does not have. The fixture is left as it is, because B10 relies on its exact files.

cases.prompt: This is demo-app. Start tracking it with TCW.

assertions.text: the agent opened the setup skill's project.md, the document for starting TCW in a repository
the agent opened no configure document: a repository with no tcw-config.yaml has nothing to configure yet
`tcw validate` is clean, so the repository is now a TCW project

cases.note: Runs on the bare fixture: a git repository with demo-app's code and no tcw-config.yaml. The seeder refuses a bare fixture inside any TCW project (any parent folder holding tcw-config.yaml), and run_evals refuses such a case before running anything, so this case can only run with --out pointing outside this checkout. In the no-skill arm no plugin is loaded, so the contains check is expected to fail there and the absent check passes trivially. project.md says to use the project name the user gave as the ID (the prompt names demo-app) and to ask otherwise; an agent that stops to ask has routed correctly but fails validate_exit_zero, so read the routing checks and the validate check separately when grading.

cases.prompt: I'm partway through {item}. Unrelated, but signing in has been taking about eight seconds for accounts with a lot of invoices, and it started right after Tuesday's invoice import. We'll need to deal with that at some point. Don't work on {item} in this turn.

assertions.text: the agent invoked the work-create skill or opened its file for an idea mentioned in passing
the agent read the work inbox while searching for overlap
the new fact (Tuesday's invoice import) reached the inbox entry that already covers the report, and nothing else changed
no item was created: the inbox entry covers the report

cases.note: The fixture seeds docs/work/inbox/slow-login.md in step 9 of seed() (evals/seed_fixture.py), which every non-bare variant runs; its text already says eight seconds for accounts with many invoices, but not the import. What tells runs apart is files_changed_exactly: an agent that ignores the remark changes nothing, and one that creates an item or a second entry changes other paths. tool_input_contains 'work-create' is also satisfied by a Bash command naming the skill folder, so it is a routing signal, not proof of behavior. In the no-skill arm the first assertion and files_changed_exactly are expected to fail. new_item_count reads items that run_one does not yet write (2026-09-15-eval-runs-under-this-checkout-grade-and-behave-wrongly).
